newsitem.title: ITALY: German dies in Alps - ninth climbing death in 24 hrs.
newsitem.headline: German dies in Alps - ninth climbing death in 24 hrs.

text.p: A 19-year-old German man died in the Italian Alps on Wednesday, the ninth mountaineering death in the region in just over 24 hours, police said.

The climber, who police did not name, died after a fall of some 100 metres (330 ft) while he was approaching the summit of the 3,480-metre (11,480 ft) Altissima mountain on the border between Austria and Italy.
His two climbing partners were unhurt.
On Tuesday, seven people fell to their deaths in two separate climbing incidents on the Great Zebru mountain near the Swiss and Austrian borders. Another climber perished on a nearby mountain.

Police in the northern Italian city of Bolzano said rescue teams were still searching for Anna Maria Neuner, 56, the wife of a senior German diplomat at the Vatican, who failed to return from a hike on Wednesday.
She was last seen on Monday near a mountain refuge where she had been lodging.
There has been a rash of climbing deaths in the Alps this summer, with more than 40 people dying in accidents in Europe's highest mountain range over the last two weeks.
